dish: keshi mochi — koshi-an wrapped in thin mochi and rolled in poppy seeds
w: Sakai confectioner founded in the Enpō era (1673–81) that still makes keshi mochi, the poppy-seed rice cake from the Nanban trade said to be a Sen no Rikyū favourite — in the Sakai city tourism guide and on ja.wikipedia.
Founded 1688; credited as the originator of nikki mochi, cinnamon-laced mochi born of Sakai's Portuguese/Spanish trade era — per ja.wikipedia (肉桂餅) and the Sakai city tourism guide.

dish: freshly ground matcha with Rikyū mochi; tea-porridge (chagayu) set
w: Tea merchant founded in Sakai in 1850 — Sen no Rikyū's hometown — whose café serves stone-ground matcha, Rikyū mochi and a tea-cuisine/tea-porridge set; featured by OSAKA-INFO and the Sakai city tourism guide.

dish: Kumamoto black-wagyu tongue and ultra-thick wagyu tenderloin (Chateaubriand)
address: Wasin Bldg 1F, 4-7 Goryōdōri, Sakai-ku, Sakai, Osaka
w: Meat master Tsuneyuki Kobayashi's yakiniku grill near Goryōmae Station, sourcing rare cuts through a private supplier network — Time Out's 20 must-go restaurants of Southern Osaka and a Tabelog Yakiniku WEST Hyakumeiten (2025) selection.

dish: tecchiri (fugu hot pot) and Kobe-beef kaiseki courses
address: 18-1 Kishiki-chō, Kishiwada, Osaka (just south of the Kishiwada Castle moat; 5 min walk from Nankai Takojizō Station)
w: 1929–39 magnate's estate on the site of the Kishiwada lords' teahouse, with three tea houses and a stroll garden, now a kaiseki restaurant in private rooms — Time Out's Southern Osaka must-go list and OSAKA-INFO.

dish: DIY charcoal seafood barbecue of just-landed octopus, conger eel (anago) and sea bream
n: Toretore Ichi (Sakai Dejima Fishing Port market)
address: Sakai Dejima Fishing Port, Sakai-ku, Sakai, Osaka
w: Weekend-only fishermen's-association market at Dejima, the old heart of Sakai's anago trade: buy fresh catch and grill it on a rented charcoal grill — OSAKA-INFO and the Sakai city tourism dining guide.
